summary: Iteration 51 — focused verification of the Global Document Design Standard. Backend: 15/15 pytest tests passed (/app/backend/tests/test_iter51_document_standard.py) covering document_renderer unit behaviour (artifact stripping, Title:/Content: -> heading/body, brand_color fallback + _logo_dominant_color from a generated PNG data URL, logo cover render), plus live PDF endpoints /api/workspace/material-pdf/{id}, /api/workspace/strategy-pdf, /api/reactivation/materials/{id}/pdf and /api/shared/{token}. Frontend: /shared/{token} and /sign/{token} both render the one standard-document layout (thin brand-color border, white bg, centered logo above centered title, org below title, black 2.0 line-height body, Created By footer); sign header no longer shows '· Version N' and signing controls are unchanged below the document. NO live AI generation was consumed (strategy verified via a temporary QA-seeded strategy material, deleted after). No signature was submitted on real data. One environment issue found and fixed: the CRA dev server was serving a STALE compiled OpportunityPages.jsx (sign page rendered the old header with '· Version 1' and no standard-document classes) — resolved by `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend`; after restart all sign-page checks pass.

minor.issue: display_text still repeats the document title as its first body line (review_routes/clean_document_text does not drop a leading duplicate title line, while refinement_routes.material_pdf explicitly does). On /shared/... 'Board Opportunity' therefore appears twice: cover title + first body line.
Uses PIL Image.getdata() which is deprecated (removal in Pillow 14) — DeprecationWarning emitted on every logo-derived brand colour; switch to get_flattened_data().

issues: The cursive typed-signature preview renders inline on the same row as, and immediately left of, the 'Sign Agreement' button, so the two visually collide once a name is typed (pre-existing, not part of this change but visible in the new standard layout)

Headings inside the body are only uppercased plain text (white-space: pre-wrap) — the PDF gets a real brand-coloured heading style while the web document has no visual heading hierarchy; consider rendering headings as elements for parity

action_items: Optional: strip the duplicate leading title line in /api/shared/{token} display_text (same rule already used in material_pdf) so the shared web document does not print its title twice
Optional: replace PIL getdata() with get_flattened_data() in document_renderer._logo_dominant_color
Optional polish: give the typed-signature preview its own row on /sign/{token} so it does not sit beside the Sign Agreement button
critical_code_review_comments: document_renderer.py is a clean single source of truth (all four PDF producers now call render_document_pdf) — no duplication found; page numbering correctly offsets the cover (getPageNumber() - 1).

clean_document_lines treats any all-uppercase line <90 chars as a heading; a body sentence written in caps (e.g. an ALL CAPS legal clause) would silently be re-styled as a heading and lose its trailing content — acceptable heuristic but worth a comment.
review_routes /shared/{token} returns branding/created_by without _id — verified no ObjectId leakage in any tested response.

Dev-server staleness: OpportunityPages.jsx edits were compiled into the bundle only after a frontend restart. Main agent should sanity-check the sign page in the browser after any further edit to that file.

rca_of_the_issue: Sign page initially rendered the pre-change markup (article class 'hosted-agreement' only, header 'Prepared for Iter16 Candidate · Version 1'). Root cause: the webpack dev server had not recompiled OpportunityPages.jsx — the served bundle contained only ONE occurrence of 'hosted-agreement-head standard-document-cover' (from SharedPages.jsx) instead of two, while line-number instrumentation still matched because the edit only added class names to existing lines. `supervisorctl restart frontend` produced a bundle with both occurrences and the page then matched the new standard exactly. No application-code defect.
